# Phase 2: exact matroid gates for a four-label transfer

Status: internally reconstructed finite obstruction and finite replay of an already
released stronger socle theorem. No justified scientific promotion.

## Interface

For a matroid M with basis set B, let S=k[y_B:B in B], let I be the kernel of
y_B -> product_{e in B} x_e, let K be generated by all degree-two binomials in I,
and let J be generated by single-element symmetric-exchange binomials.
The remaining quadratic White interface is I=K. It is NOT I=J: Larson's
July 2026 primary paper supplies a counterexample to the latter.

The release CM tensor proof's combinatorial reduction, hodge-02-tensors.tex
lines388–401, corrects independent sign columns by two-row swaps. Its
composition, lines418–455, contracts auxiliary tensor factors and divides by
nonzero scalar values q_i in Qbar*. Neither step requires treating the claimed
class-wide Hodge theorem as validated for the present examination.

Two candidate transfer gates were attacked:
(A) fixed-target greedy correction remains available when allowed rows are
matroid bases;
(B) legal paths after adding auxiliary rows can be cancelled back in the
polynomial ideal.

Both gates fail.

## A. An exact Fano greedy counterexample

Use the Fano matroid of rank3 on labels0,…,6, where label i is the nonzero
binary vector with integer code i+1. A triple is a basis exactly when its
three binary vectors are independent. It has28 bases.

Let A={013,024,156}, B={016,025,134}; notation013 means {0,1,3}.
Each is a multiset of three bases. Their ground-set incidence counts agree:
(2,2,1,1,1,1,1).

For multisets U,V of p bases, define
D(U,V)=min_permutations sum_i |U_i \ V_pi(i)|.
It allows free relabelling of rows, making the fixed-target greedy claim
stronger than a particular chosen row ordering. D(A,B)=3.

A legal quadratic move replaces ANY pair of bases by ANY other pair with the
same multiset ground-set union. Direct exact enumeration of all such moves
from A gives precisely the following seven distinct neighbors:

| Neighbor | D(neighbor,B) |
|---|---:|
| {013,014,256} |3|
| {013,015,246} |4|
| {013,026,145} |3|
| {013,045,126} |3|
| {013,046,125} |3|
| {014,023,156} |3|
| {015,024,136} |3|

Thus no legal arbitrary quadratic move strictly decreases D. This attacks
the remaining weak White interface, rather than only single-element moves.

# Phase 2 independent combinatorial attempt

**Outcome: no justified promotion.** One opportunity was tested: transfer the
release CM proof's four-label switch-and-contraction mechanism to the remaining
quadratic-generation form of White's matroid conjecture. The attempt produced
two concrete obstruction gates and a finite replay of a previously released
stronger result.

The release mechanism was used at its technical interface, not by assuming the
claimed CM Hodge theorem. Its coordinate correction permits all odd sign rows;
matroid bases form a restricted row domain. Its auxiliary contraction returns
nonzero scalars, which can be divided out. Polynomial basis variables do not
have this property.

## Actual attacks

1. **Fixed-target correction is false.** In the Fano rank3 matroid, take
A={013,024,156} and B={016,025,134}, with label i representing binary vector
i+1. The multisets have equal incidence counts. Their minimum row-matching
deficit is3. All seven arbitrary two-base replacement neighbors have deficit
at least3, so no strictly decreasing quadratic move exists. A verified
3-step path has deficits3,3,2,0. This refutes the proposed greedy gate, not
quadratic connectivity itself.

2. **Auxiliary cancellation is false.** Reconstructing Larson's published
rank9 binary matrix gives14,848 bases and2,784 unordered complementary pairs.
The symmetric-exchange graph has two components of sizes864 and1,920.
For the published low/high relation f, exact cubic paths show every basis
variable y_N satisfies y_N f in J while f is outside J, where J is generated
by symmetric-exchange quadrics. Thus J:f is the irrelevant maximal ideal.
The same-context generator and a separate dense-binary/codeword certificate
checker agree on this complete finite statement. They do not constitute
external validation or formal kernel replay.

Historical checking then found the exact stronger prior art: Taeseok Oh's
July31,2026 cyclic-family socle theorem. Its primary proof already establishes
this annihilation for all parameters, including Larson's example. The finite
construction is a replay, not a new result.
